title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 217 (Agent’s right of retainer out of sums received on principal’s account)

content.overview: An agent may retain, out of any sums received on account of the principal in the business of the agency, all moneys due to himself in respect of advances made or expenses properly incurred by him in conducting such business, and also such remuneration as may be payable to him for acting as agent.
content.glance: Agent may retain from principal’s moneys: advances, proper expenses, and payable remuneration.
content.study: An agent may retain, out of any sums received on account of the principal in the business of the agency, all moneys due to himself in respect of advances made or expenses properly incurred by him in conducting such business, and also such remuneration as may be payable to him for acting as agent. Subject to this retainer, s. 218 requires payment of the balance to the principal.

sections.heading: Sums received on principal’s account
sections.body: Sums received on account of the principal in the business of the agency.

sections.heading: Retain advances and proper expenses
sections.body: Moneys due for advances made or expenses properly incurred.

sections.heading: Retain payable remuneration
sections.body: Such remuneration as may be payable for acting as agent.

provisions.title: Agent’s right of retainer out of sums received on principal’s account

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 217 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Identify sums received; test advances, proper expenses and remuneration; apply retainer; then s. 218 for the balance.

examTips: Retainer for advances, expenses and remuneration.
